findings.situation: A filer's 2025 W-2 shows code AA twice in box 12: a 2025 designated Roth contribution and a USERRA make-up contribution for 2024 (e.g., "AA 24 1250.00"), and the filer enters the total of both.
findings.source_text: iw2w3 p. 20: "If any elective deferrals ... during the year are make-up amounts under ... (USERRA) for a prior year, you must enter the prior-year contributions separately. Beginning with the earliest year, enter the code, the year, and the amount."; f8880 p. 1, line 2: "Elective deferrals to a 401(k) or other qualified employer plan ... for 2025"
findings.why: The question "Form W-2 box 12, code AA ... zero if none" and its help do not tell the filer to leave out code AA entries marked with a prior year. A truthful answer can therefore include prior-year make-up contributions, but Form 8880 line 2 counts only contributions for 2025.

findings.why: The instructions say these amounts 'may' appear in box 12. No box 12 code covers after-tax voluntary employee contributions, so a question limited to the listed box 12 codes cannot capture them, and line 2 is understated.

findings.situation: A filer's box 12 shows more than one code G entry because some 457(b) contributions are USERRA make-up amounts for earlier years (for example 'G 24 1250.00' plus 'G 7000.00'), and the filer must decide which to enter.
findings.source_text: iw2w3 p. 20: "If any elective deferrals, salary reduction amounts, or nonelective contributions under a section 457(b) plan during the year are make-up amounts under ... (USERRA) for a prior year, you must enter the prior-year contributions separately. Beginning with the earliest year, enter the code, the year, and the amount."
findings.why: The question and help ask for 'the code G amount' as if there is a single entry. One filer may enter only the undated current-year entry and another may add every code G entry, so the gate gets different values. The gate compares the elective part with this amount, and a filer whose elective part includes make-up amounts could trip it when the box 12 total was not entered.

findings.situation: A filer who worked for a railroad employer and another employer in 2025 had tier 1 RRTA tax withheld, which appears in W-2 box 14 rather than box 4, so a truthful box 4 answer leaves it out.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 117, Line 11: "too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld. You can take a credit on this line for the amount withheld in excess of $10,918.20."
findings.why: The per-person total and the per-employer over-limit test must count tier 1 RRTA withholding together with social security tax. The question asks only for box 4 social security tax, so the total understates the excess and misses a railroad employer that withheld more than the limit.

findings.situation: A filer whose wage statement is Form 499R-2/W-2PR (Puerto Rico) reports Medicare wages and tips in box 22, but a truthful answer to 'Form W-2 box 5' gives that form's box 5 instead, so the Medicare wages line 1 needs are left out.
findings.source_text: i8959 p. 1: "References to Form W-2 on Form 8959 and in these instructions also apply to Forms W-2AS, W-2CM, W-2GU, W-2VI, and 499R-2/W-2PR. However, for Form 499R-2/W-2PR, Medicare wages and tips are reported in box 22"
findings.why: The question and its help name only box 5. They do not mention the territory forms or the box 22 alternative, so a filer with a 499R-2/W-2PR would leave out the Medicare wages line 1 requires.

locators: Form 8959 (2025), line 1, "Medicare wages and tips from Form W-2, box 5", "enter the total of the amounts from box 5";

findings.situation: A filer's Form W-2 shows uncollected Medicare tax on tips in box 12 code B, or uncollected Medicare tax on group-term life insurance in box 12 code N; line 19 needs those amounts, but the question asks only for box 6 and the helper adds only w2.box6.
findings.source_text: i8959 (2025) p. 4, Line 19: "Also include any uncollected Medicare tax on tips from Form W-2, box 12, code B, and any uncollected Medicare tax on the taxable cost of group-term life insurance over $50,000 (for former employees) from Form W-2, box 12, code N."
findings.why: A truthful box 6 amount leaves out the code B and code N amounts that the instructions add to line 19. Line 22 then understates Additional Medicare Tax withholding.

findings.situation: A filer with a Puerto Rico Form 499R-2/W-2PR reports Medicare tax withheld in box 23, but the question asks for box 6, so a literal answer gives the wrong box.
findings.source_text: i8959 (2025) p. 1, Reminders: "for Form 499R-2/W-2PR, Medicare wages and tips are reported in box 22 and Medicare tax withheld is reported in box 23."
findings.why: Neither the question nor its help tells W-2PR filers to use box 23. They would enter box 6 of that form, which is not Medicare tax withheld.

locators: Form 8959 (2025), line 19, "Medicare tax withheld from Form W-2, box 6", "enter the total of the amounts from box 6";

findings.situation: An employee whose box 3 wages plus reported tips exceed $176,100 has a box 7 figure smaller than the tips they actually reported, and could answer with either number.
findings.source_text: iw2w3 (2025) p. 18, Box 7: "Show the tips that the employee reported to you... The total of boxes 3 and 7 should not be more than $176,100 (the maximum social security wage base for 2025)."
findings.why: The help calls box 7 both 'Box 7 of this Form W-2' and 'the tips you reported to this employer.' When the wage-base cap applies, these differ, and a filer who enters total reported tips would overstate the box 3 plus 7 social security wages the excess-tax lines need.
